__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus that scrapes /api/v1/public/metrics on your ProxCenter.

description: Multi-cluster Proxmox VE fleet: reachability, capacity headroom, guest load and HA state, across every cluster one ProxCenter manages. Scrapes ProxCenter's own aggregated exposition, so a single Prometheus job covers every cluster without an agent on any node. Requires ProxCenter Enterprise with the API option.

panels.title: Clusters
panels.description: Every PVE connection ProxCenter manages, clustered or standalone.

panels.title: Nodes offline
panels.description: The actionable half of the pair: anything above zero is a node the fleet lost.

panels.title: Guests running
panels.description: Templates are excluded upstream, so this counts real workloads only.

panels.title: ProxCenter
panels.description: Version of the ProxCenter being scraped.

panels.title: Memory free per node
panels.description: Free memory as a share of the node's own capacity. A ratio rather than a byte count on purpose: 20 GiB free is comfortable on a 24 GiB node and critical on a 1 TiB one, so an absolute threshold cannot be right for both.

panels.title: Root filesystem usage
panels.description: The HOST root filesystem, not cluster storage. A full root filesystem is what stops a node accepting migrations.

panels.title: Ceph health across clusters

defaults.noValue: No Ceph cluster in this selection

panels.description: Clusters without Ceph emit nothing, so they are absent rather than counted as unknown.

panels.title: Cluster health
panels.description: A degraded cluster has lost quorum or a node. Green is the healthy state, so a coloured band here is always something to look at.

panels.title: Node uptime, longest first
panels.description: A node up far longer than its peers is a node that has missed the reboots its peers took.

panels.title: Memory overcommit
panels.description: Memory promised to guests against memory that exists. Above 1 the fleet depends on the balloon driver handing memory back, which a Windows guest without free page reporting will not do.

panels.title: Peak memory per node
panels.description: The peak over the selected window. A node sitting at 60 per cent that peaked at 95 nearly ran out, and the current value never shows it.

panels.title: Root filesystem in seven days
panels.description: Where each root filesystem lands in seven days at the current trend. Needs several hours of history to mean anything, so read it as a direction and not as a date.

panels.title: Cluster availability over the window
panels.description: Share of the selected window during which each cluster answered. Anything short of 1 is a gap the instantaneous tiles at the top cannot show.

panels.title: Nodes that changed state

defaults.noValue: No node changed state in this window

panels.description: A node that bounced overnight reads as online on the tile above, exactly like one that never moved. This counts the transitions.

panels.title: Nodes that rebooted

defaults.noValue: No node rebooted in this window

panels.description: An uptime that goes backwards is a reboot. Counted over the window without going through the task log.

panels.title: Guests that changed state

defaults.noValue: No guest changed state in this window

panels.description: Guests that stopped and restarted on their own. A guest in a crash loop shows the same running state as a stable one on any instantaneous count.

panels.title: Guest memory, allocated against in use
panels.description: The gap between the two lines is the overcommit a balloon driver is expected to absorb.

panels.title: Guests by HA state

defaults.noValue: No guest is managed by HA

panels.description: Guests HA does not manage emit nothing at all, so this counts only the HA estate.

panels.title: Guests in HA error

defaults.noValue: No guest is in HA error

panels.description: An HA resource in error has stopped being managed: HA will not restart or relocate it until an operator clears the state.

panels.title: Guest agent inventory
Guests without the guest agent enabled

defaults.noValue: No data yet on this install

panels.description: No data yet on most installs, and that is expected rather than broken. ProxCenter builds its inventory from /cluster/resources, which carries no guest agent config flag, so the flag is unknown and the series is deliberately omitted rather than published as a misleading zero. It fills in once the agent flag has a source, which means a capped pass over /config.
Collapsed on purpose: the series behind it is empty on most installs today. Open the row to read why.
